subject: Quantis: live feed — intermittent chunked silence causing throughput loss
messages:
From: Ellen Shaw <ellen.shaw@quantishealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: support@quantishealth.com
Date: 2027-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production: live transcript feed stalls, spikes in latency and 502s

Jonas — urgent. Over the last 45 minutes our live transcription channel for patient intake has been intermittently stopping to emit chunks for ~20-45s, then resuming with a long burst (lots of tokens at once). We’re seeing: 
- Average per-token latency jump from 0.12s to ~1.8s
- 5xx error spikes around 4.8% of requests (previously ~0.2%)
- Throughput drop: peak concurrent sessions limited by long tail freezes.

We have customer-facing SLAs and clinical workflows are being delayed. Attached are three compressed capture files and a short screen capture of the client-side behavior. We can join a bridge immediately.

Request: escalation to on-call SRE and someone who owns streaming infra.

Thanks,
Ellen
Director, Engineering
Quantis Health

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Ellen Shaw <ellen.shaw@quantishealth.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-07T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: live transcript feed stalls, spikes in latency and 502s

Joined the bridge — initial read: logs show a pattern consistent with proxy backpressure + connection keepalive timeouts. Observations: 
- Multiple upstream keepalive resets at ~30s causing mid-stream silence; client then re-sends and we get an immediate backlog (burst of tokens).
- Error type: intermittent 502/504 from our edge proxies, correlates with sustained CPU spikes on a subset of GPU hosts handling Quantis routes.
- Batching: some requests show huge batch accumulation (~200ms queuing) followed by a DOS-like token flush.

Short mitigations we can flip now: 
1) Reduce server-side max batch window from 200ms -> 60ms for Quantis routes (low-risk, limited perf cost).
2) Force fallback to the lower-memory model variant for sessions older than 30s (reduces KV pressure).
3) Enforce 15s TCP keepalive probes on the proxy tier to prevent long silent disconnect gaps.

I’ll push a canary for (1) and (3) now; (2) requires a quick config change (will push in 15m if metrics look good). Please send any request IDs you have — I’m cross-referencing with trace ids in the tarball.

Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: keppel-keepalive-patches.diff.txt

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Ellen Shaw <ellen.shaw@quantishealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-08T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: live transcript feed stalls, spikes in latency and 502s — update and next steps

Ellen / Tom — final update after the hotfix and canary rollout:
- What we changed: reduced server batch window to 60ms for your tenant, enabled 15s keepalive probes on proxy tier, and partially rolled model-variant fallback for sessions older than 45s.
- Observed improvement: 5xx error rate dropped from 4.8% -> 0.3% over the 3h observation window; median per-token latency returned to ~0.14s; throughput normalized to pre-incident levels.
- Root cause (prelim): a scheduling regression in the proxy pool combined with a rare combination of long-lived sessions caused asymmetric queue buildup. The proxy would tear keepalive and the backend would then flush a backlog creating large token bursts.

Next steps:
1) We’ll run a full postmortem and share no later than 2027-06-09 EOD (draft attached).
2) Engineering: permanent fix for proxy scheduling + capacity hedging for tenants with many concurrent long-lived sessions.
3) Commercial: Marissa will coordinate emergency credits; Jonas will follow up with Quantis for the formal SLA remediation.

Thanks for your patience; let us know if you see any further regressions.

— Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem_draft_quantis_20270608.md
